newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Suicide suspected in S.Korean banker's death.
newsitem.headline: Suicide suspected in S.Korean banker's death.

text.p: A former South Korean banker embroiled in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal was found hanged at his home on Monday and police said they suspected suicide.

Park Suk-tae was an executive director of the Korea First Bank, the main creditor of failed Hanbo Steel Co at the centre of the scandal. He was called in for questioning at a parliamentary inquiry this month.
Park quit the bank in March after he was warned by the state Office of Bank Supervision that the bank's loans to Hanbo were not backed by sufficient collateral, a bank spokesman said.
A police officer quoted Park's family members as saying he frequently talked of death after he testified in parliament on April 17.
Hanbo Steel Co collapsed in January under the weight of $5.8 billion of debts.
Eleven people, including bankers, senior politicians and Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo are now on trial for bribery in connection with the scandal.
